title: Visibility Is Not Detection: Auditing Observation Boundaries in Long-Horizon AI Evaluation
thesis: Long-horizon evaluation validity depends on auditing the observation surface itself: controlled perturbations expose family-specific visibility blind spots, hierarchy alone does not guarantee diagnosability, and cross-dataflow transfer fails when visibility and detection measurement objects are not causally aligned.

claims.claim: Visibility, detection and harmfulness are distinct constructs and the frozen evaluator has family-specific observation boundaries.

Single-responsive-leaf flat/hierarchical scores are affine/rank-equivalent and clean-only matched-FPR equality is not identifiable; explicit stage-aligned instrumentation is required for controlled localization.
Cross-dataflow transfer requires causal alignment of measurement objects; the current FinQA v2 result is a failed-transfer/measurement-object-mismatch autopsy, not protocol blindness.

forbidden_claims: universal blind spots across AI systems
